answer: I'd like to talk about a moment when I surprised myself by staying calm. A time I managed to stay calm under real pressure was during a minor emergency at a family gathering, when my grandfather suddenly felt faint. It happened last Eid at my grandparents' village home, where the whole family had gathered for lunch. It was a very hot afternoon, and he had been busy greeting guests all morning. There was an immediate sense of alarm among everyone, and the atmosphere quickly became [[chaotic]], with people shouting advice from every direction. For some reason, I felt a strange sense of clarity and knew someone had to [[take charge]]. I calmly helped him sit down in the shade, brought water, and reassured everyone while we decided whether to call the local doctor. I also asked the children to step back and give him some air. My younger sister ran to fetch a hand fan, which helped a lot. Staying [[composed]] was not easy, because I love him dearly, but I knew that adding to the panic would only make things worse. Thankfully, he recovered within a few minutes, and it turned out he was simply tired and dehydrated. Afterwards, several relatives told me how [[reassuring]] my calmness had been, which surprised me. Honestly, I had not known I was capable of keeping such a level head. That experience taught me that staying [[rational]] in a crisis is a genuinely valuable ability, and it gave me more confidence in myself. My grandmother still mentions it whenever the family gets together.

followUps.answer: Yes, thankfully. He is in his eighties but still remarkably sharp and active. Since that day, though, we make sure he rests more and drinks plenty of water, especially during the hot months.

followUps.q: Do you think staying calm can be learned?
followUps.answer: I think so, at least partly. Some people are naturally calmer, but practice and experience help a lot. The more difficult situations you face, the less likely you are to panic.
